text:
leo: Heads up — since ~03:12 UTC I'm seeing trace->log join rate drop for eu-west-1 GPU nodes. Jaeger traces have trace_id but Loki queries for the same trace_id return nothing. Correlation SLO looks ~85% degraded for the last 3h. @oncall?

anika: Can you paste the exact Loki query you're running?

leo: Sure. Quick example I'm running in Grafana Explore (Loki):
```
{app="inference-runtime", cluster="eu-west-1"} |= "trace_id=" | json | trace_id="<trace-id>"
```
Returns nothing for traces that definitely exist in Jaeger.

jonas: saw an alert earlier from the pipeline:
`sre-bot: [ALERT] trace-join-rate-drop firing for eu-west-1 (since 03:10 UTC)`

sre-bot: alert: trace-join-rate-drop; severity=warning; cluster=eu-west-1; observed=14% correlated (target=99.9%)

maria: Any recent agent/fluentd/filebeat changes in eu-west-1? We had a filebeat bump yesterday to enable HTTP compression when shipping to Loki ingest. That could mangle boundaries if not handled.

leo: That's what I'm suspecting. Quick dump from one node's /var/log/pods shows some binary-ish headers in the stream: `\x1f\x8b` present at the start of some entries (gzip magic).

anika: If the forwarder started gzipping batches, Loki/promtail might be seeing compressed payloads as single huge line or as binary and then our `json` stage in query fails. Check promtail `pipeline_stages` and `multiline` config on the agent. Also check the HTTP content-encoding header on the push to Loki.

jonas: I can repro locally: when compression is enabled without the expected Content-Encoding header, Loki stores raw compressed blobs as a single line. Our queries that expect JSON lines won't match.

maria: Actionable checks:
- `kubectl exec` into promtail pod and curl the push endpoint to see headers
- look at filebeat change: bump 7.14 -> 7.15 in eu-west-1; check the commit that enabled `http_compression: true`
- run `hexdump -C` on a sample file from the node to confirm gzip magic

leo: I'm running `kubectl logs` on a few sidecars now to confirm. If compression is the culprit we can rollback the filebeat change for the eu-west pool.

anika: Also a useful temporary workaround: query traces in Jaeger and use span metadata (service, pod, host) to locate logs by host+container rather than trace_id. More noise but will recover most joins for the last 6h until we backfill.

jonas: For a targeted Loki query to find compressed records we can search for the gzip magic in raw lines: `|~ "\\x1f\\x8b"` (Grafana escapes fun) — that should show which streams have binary/blobs.

maria: Cost note: if we backfill the 6h window by re-ingesting or running heavy queries across shards, we will spike Loki query and storage costs. Keep finance in the loop if we plan reindex/backfill.

leo: Update — confirmed on node gpu-eu-12: filebeat is sending compressed payloads and Content-Encoding header is missing due to the sidecar proxy (envoy filter) removing the header. So Loki received compressed payload as raw text.

anika: Ok that explains it. Two immediate fixes:
- Quick rollback of the filebeat http_compression flag for eu-west-1 (low blast radius) — leo can coordinate.
- Short-term query fallback: use Jaeger->span->host join for critical traces.

jonas: Long term: add explicit label enrichment at ingestion so trace_id is extracted by promtail/filebeat before compression, or ensure the forwarder preserves Content-Encoding header through envoy. Also add an alert on "trace_id present in span but missing in logs" (we already have one but needs tuning).

maria: I'll open a PR to change our promtail pipeline to attempt gzip sniffing and decompress if we detect magic header. That could be a safe guard.

leo: Rolling back filebeat now on a single node to validate. Will post results in ~10m.

(10m) leo: Rolled back on gpu-eu-12. After ~2 minutes I see join rate for that host go from 12% -> 98% correlated for new traces. Good sign.

anika: Nice. Can you also capture an example compressed payload and attach to the incident? Useful for the promtail PR.

leo: Attached sample (in the incident ticket).

jonas: Next steps / action items:
- leo: rollback across fleet in a controlled way, monitor Loki query errors and join rate (ETA 30m)
- maria: promtail PR to detect/decompress gzip blobs and/or extract trace_id pre-compression
- anika: update the SLO alert to lower noise and add a runbook link for trace-log joins
- jonas: follow up with infra networking team to patch envoy so it preserves Content-Encoding header

maria: FYI I'll also add a short-term Grafana panel that shows % of traces with log joins per cluster so we get visual alerts earlier.

leo: I'll open INC-2026-45 and assign followups. Thanks all — looks like compression+envoy header loss is the root cause. Will post a short postmortem after the rollout. :thumbsup:
